author: product-requirements-expert
title: Staff can correct a booked visit's date and description
summary: A booked visit can be opened for correction, prefilled with its current date and description, and saved back over the same visit. The pet gains no second visit record.
acceptance_criteria: Opening a booked visit for correction shows the booking form carrying that visit's current date and description.
Submitting a description and a date later than today updates that visit and shows the owner's record.
After a saved correction the pet has the same number of visits it had before.
Submitting a blank description refuses the change, names the description, and shows the form again.
Submitting a date of today or earlier refuses the change, names the date, and shows the form again.
A correction addressed to a visit that is not the named pet's is refused rather than applied.
A refused correction leaves the stored visit exactly as it was.
non_goals: Cancelling or deleting a booked visit (NG-5, NG-4).
Any link to the correction form from the owner's record — the owner deferred the entry point to a possible follow-up request.
Changing which pet a visit belongs to.
notes: Narrowing recorded in docs/adr/2026-08-31-non-goal-visit-correction.md; the 2026-08-08 non-goal ADR now points forward to it. The ADR index row in docs/adr/README.md is outside my write scope — system-design-expert should add: 2026-08-31 | Correcting a Booked Visit Is In Scope; Cancelling Stays Out | Accepted. Three open questions recorded in the PRD rather than answered: the missing entry point, whether a past-dated visit can be corrected at all under the future-date rule, and whether the correction form shows the pet's other visits. The dispatch settled none of them and stated no further product answer will come.

scope_overrides.owner_decision: Non-goal NG-5 is narrowed: cancelling a booked visit stays out of scope, but correcting a booked visit's date and description is now in scope.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: Visit correction is the pet-correction pattern applied to the third child of the owner aggregate. PetController.processUpdateForm/updatePetDetails (PetController.java:139-200) already demonstrates it: load the aggregate root, find the child by its path identifier, write the submitted values onto the stored child, save through OwnerRepository. Nothing new is needed in package structure, dependencies, persistence, or validation. One existing element needs adjusting: VisitController's class-level @ModelAttribute("visit") loadPetWithVisit runs before every handler in the controller and unconditionally constructs a fresh Visit and calls pet.addVisit(visit) (VisitController.java:63-81). Left as it is, the correction GET would render a blank form and the correction POST would attach a second visit to the pet. The adjustment mirrors PetController.findPet (PetController.java:75-87): take visitId as an optional path variable, return the stored visit from the pet when it is present, and take the new-visit branch only when it is absent. docs/system-design.md Contracts is updated for the three rows this touches, and the aggregate invariant now states that a correction writes over the visit the pet already holds. Basis is grep and direct file reads; the IntelliJ oracle is not connected in this run.
integration_points: GET and POST /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit are added to VisitController; the two /visits/new routes keep their current behaviour unchanged.
loadPetWithVisit becomes visitId-aware and stays the single loader for both flows; the existing owner and pet lookups and their IllegalArgumentException refusals are reused.
The write path stays OwnerRepository.save on the owner aggregate; no VisitRepository is introduced (docs/system-design.md Overview, Contracts).
The @InitBinder disallowing id and *.id stays as it is; the corrected visit keeps its identity from the loaded entity, not from the form.

createOrUpdateVisitForm.html posts to its own URL with no action attribute, so it serves the correction POST unchanged; its heading and previous-visits table already branch on whether the visit is new.

patterns.description: updatePetDetails: locate the existing child inside the aggregate by id, copy the submitted values onto it, save the root. The visit correction is the same shape with two fields.
findPet: a @ModelAttribute loader taking an optional path identifier, returning the stored child when the id is present and a fresh instance when it is not. This is the shape loadPetWithVisit adopts.
the future-date rejection for a booked visit. The correction reuses it verbatim, including the typeMismatch.visitDate message key; @NotBlank on Visit.description covers the description rule.

risks.risk: The correction POST attaches a second visit to the pet, breaking the acceptance criterion that the visit count is unchanged. Pet.visits is a LinkedHashSet with cascade ALL and BaseEntity does not override equals, so a second instance carrying the same id would still be added and cascaded.
risks.mitigation: Never call pet.addVisit on the correction path. Bind onto, or copy onto, the instance already inside pet.getVisits(); assert the count before and after in the test named for it.

risks.risk: A correction addressed to a visit that is not the named pet's is applied to the wrong record (PRD edge case 3).
risks.mitigation: Resolve visitId strictly by walking owner.getPet(petId).getVisits(); refuse a miss with the same IllegalArgumentException shape the loader already uses for an unknown pet. Cover it with a test.

risks.risk: A refused correction leaves the stored visit altered (PRD edge case 4). Binding writes the submitted values onto the loaded instance before validation runs.
risks.mitigation: The instance is detached — spring.jpa.open-in-view is disabled and the owner is loaded outside a transaction — and the error branch returns the view without calling owners.save. Keep the save strictly after the hasErrors check, and assert the stored visit is untouched by re-reading it in the test.

risks.risk: A new message key added for a correction-specific button or heading fails the build. I18nPropertiesSyncTest compares keys across all eleven bundles, and REQ-LANG-002 forbids a partly translated language.
risks.mitigation: Reuse the existing keys. The template already varies its heading on visit['new'] and the addVisit button label needs no change for this slice; adding a key means adding and translating it in all eleven bundles.

risks.risk: The correction form lists the visit being corrected in its own previous-visits table, which the PRD leaves as an open question.
risks.mitigation: Narrowest reading: leave the template's list behaviour as it is. The table iterates pet.visits and filters new instances only; no change is in scope.

notes: Verdict is minor, not new: no new pattern, module, dependency, or persistence shape appears, so the ADR bar is not met. The product decision is already recorded in docs/adr/2026-08-31-non-goal-visit-correction.md by product-requirements-expert. Durable-memory writes this dispatch: docs/adr/README.md gains the index row for that ADR; docs/system-design.md Contracts wires REQ-VIS-003 into the Owner, Visit, OwnerRepository, and VisitController rows and restates the VisitController purpose, and the invariants paragraph gains the write-over-in-place statement. No design-doc-autofix records exist in the log, so the autofix audit is empty. Out of scope and not fixed here, per dispatch: the doctor failure project-data: spec_version 0.1.0 does not match manifest 0.2.0 in scripts/layout.toml, which predates this slice. No entry point from the owner detail page is added — the routes are URL-reachable only, matching the PRD and the ADR's open question. Existing security posture is unchanged: the routes are unauthenticated like every other route (docs/system-design.md Security Context), the id-binding guard stays, and the refusal path reveals only identifiers already present in the URL.

author: code-quality-reviewer

findings.location: VisitController.java:98 findVisit(Pet pet, int petId, int visitId)
findings.description: `petId` is passed alongside `pet` purely to build the exception message, even though `Pet` already exposes `getId()` (inherited from `BaseEntity`) and the caller at line 86 always passes the very `petId` used to look up `pet`. Carrying both invites the two to drift (e.g. a future caller passing a `pet` looked up under a different id) and adds a parameter the method doesn't need.
findings.fix: Drop the `petId` parameter and build the message from `pet.getId()` instead: `private Visit findVisit(Pet pet, int visitId)` ... `"Visit with id " + visitId + " not found for pet with id " + pet.getId() + "."`; update the call site at line 86 to `findVisit(pet, visitId)`.

approved_aspects: loadPetWithVisit follows the PetController.findPet precedent exactly: visitId is an optional @PathVariable, the stored visit is returned when present, and pet.addVisit(new Visit()) only fires on the booking branch — the design-block's requirement that the correction path never call addVisit is met.
findVisit correctly refuses another pet's visit with a clear IllegalArgumentException carrying both ids.

processUpdateVisitForm uses @ModelAttribute(name = "owner", binding = false) to close the mass-assignment hole, and owners.save sits strictly after the hasErrors check so a refused correction never touches the repository.
VIEWS_VISITS_CREATE_OR_UPDATE_FORM extracted as a constant mirrors PetController's VIEWS_PETS_CREATE_OR_UPDATE_FORM naming exactly.
Javadoc on loadPetWithVisit and findVisit clearly states the correction-vs-booking distinction for the next reader.
checkFormat passes clean; no formatting violations found.
Test class uses well-named constants (BOOKED_VISIT_DATE, CORRECTED_VISIT_DESCRIPTION, etc.) and BDD-style test names that read as behavior statements.

author: security-reviewer

findings.description: Pre-existing, out-of-slice, already recorded in .scratch/escalations.md item 1. Class sweep for 'handler binds an aggregate root from a form-bound @ModelAttribute and then saves it' finds exactly three remaining instances, all outside this slice: VisitController.processNewVisitForm (`@ModelAttribute Owner owner`, saved at :133), PetController.processCreationForm (`Owner owner` at :108, saveAndFlush at :126), PetController.processUpdateForm (`Owner owner` at :145, saveAndFlush at :199). On each, a POST carrying `lastName`, `firstName`, `address`, `city`, or `telephone` overwrites the owner's stored details as a side effect. OwnerController.processUpdateOwnerForm (:145) binds the owner deliberately and is not an instance. Security classification: MEDIUM-as-written, LOW in this application's actual threat model. It is an integrity defect (an unexpected write reachable from an unrelated form), not a privilege-boundary crossing: docs/system-design.md Security Context records no authentication, authorization, or CSRF anywhere, so any caller who can reach these routes can already POST /owners/{id}/edit directly and change the same fields with no extra effort. The exposure adds no capability an attacker lacks. It therefore does not warrant blocking this slice, and the fix (`@ModelAttribute(name = "owner", binding = false)`, the one applied here) changes three existing routes' behaviour and needs its own tests. The open question is a product one and belongs to the PRD owner: open a defect requirement covering the three handlers, or record acceptance against NG-1 with the reasoning above. No security objection to either answer.

approved_aspects: IDOR / object ownership is enforced end to end on the new path. loadPetWithVisit resolves owner by ownerId, then pet via owner.getPet(petId) (which walks only that owner's pets and returns null for a foreign pet, refused at :78), then visit via findVisit walking only pet.getVisits(). A visitId belonging to another pet or another owner cannot reach the handler, and the test theVisitCorrectionShouldBeRefusedWhenTheVisitIsNotTheNamedPets pins it with owners.save asserted never called. There is no cross-owner or cross-pet read or write path.

Failure mode is safe. The refusal throws IllegalArgumentException from a @ModelAttribute method, yielding HTTP 500 on error.html, consistent with the pre-existing owner-not-found and pet-not-found refusals. The message interpolates only visitId and petId, which are int/Integer path variables the caller itself supplied and which fail path binding if non-numeric — so no internal state is disclosed and there is no reflected-XSS vector (Thymeleaf th:text escapes, and Spring Boot's server.error.include-message default of `never` is not overridden in application.properties). The known defect 'the error page renders the exception message' is unchanged by this slice and leaks nothing new here.

Mass assignment is fully closed on the new path. The controller-wide unnamed @InitBinder setAllowedFields (:54-57) disallows `id` and `*.id` on every binder in VisitController, so the `visit` model attribute — which is the stored entity from pet.getVisits(), not a copy — cannot have its identifier rebound to another visit's id. Visit declares only `date` and `description` beyond BaseEntity.id, so no other field is over-bindable. On processUpdateVisitForm the owner is additionally `binding = false`, and theVisitCorrectionShouldChangeNothingButTheVisit proves lastName/city submitted alongside the correction do not reach the saved owner.

Refused corrections leave stored state untouched, and the claim survives inspection rather than resting on the comment. owners.save sits strictly after the hasErrors return. Request binding does mutate the loaded Visit instance in place, but spring.jpa.open-in-view=false means the graph is detached when findById returns, so no dirty-checking flush can persist the refused values; @Cacheable appears only on VetRepository, so no shared Owner instance is cached and mutated across requests; and no Hibernate second-level cache is configured. theRefusedVisitCorrectionShouldLeaveTheStoredVisitAsItWas covers the behaviour, and the per-lookup fresh graph in the test fixture models the detached repository correctly.

No injection surface added: no SQL, no string-concatenated query, no file or path operation, no deserialization, no command execution, no reflection. Data access stays on Spring Data JPA derived methods.

No secrets in the diff. Swept the change set for credential-shaped names (token, password, secret, key, credential, passwd, apikey, authorization) — no hits in either changed source file; the only literals added are view names, message codes, and test fixture data.

Supply chain unchanged: build.gradle and the Maven POM are not in the change set and no dependency, plugin, or repository coordinate is added or moved. No dependencyCheck plugin is configured in build.gradle, so dependencyCheckAnalyze has no task to run; there is no new third-party code to scan for this slice.

The new route inherits the application-wide no-authentication / no-CSRF posture already recorded in the system-design threat model and NG-1. It adds a second state-changing route on a surface where every mutating POST is already open, so it introduces no new class of exposure — noted for completeness, not raised as a finding against this slice.

author: test-reviewer

findings.description: The reload-and-compare half of this test cannot fail independent of the never().save() assertion in the same test. init() stubs owners.findById(TEST_OWNER_ID) with willAnswer(() -> ownerWithABookedVisit()), which builds a brand-new Owner/Pet/Visit graph on every invocation. The second GET therefore always returns a pristine visit regardless of what the POST mutated in-memory on the first request's (separate) object graph — there is no shared state through which a persistence-side regression could leak into the reload. The only load-bearing assertion in this test is then(this.owners).should(never()).save(...), which test theVisitCorrectionShouldRedisplayTheFormWhenTheDescriptionIsBlank already covers with the same input. Either give the stub a single shared Owner instance across findById calls so the reload genuinely observes in-memory mutation state, or drop the reload/reassert lines and rely on the never(save) assertion, which is what actually pins the invariant.
findings.fix: Change init() to stash one Owner instance in a field and have findById return that same instance on every call (only for this test, or via a dedicated stateful fake), so a bug that skips the hasErrors() guard and calls save() unconditionally — or one that mutates the stored visit before validation runs — is actually observable on reload. Alternatively, remove the redundant reload assertions and keep only the never(save) check, renaming the test to reflect that narrower scope.

findings.description: The tampering values "Tampered" (lastName and city params) are bare string literals with no named constant, violating the Three-Tier Data Naming convention (testing-principles.md) for tests written from 2026-07-31 onward. The value is meaningful — it exists specifically to prove mass-assignment binding did not occur — so it belongs in a role-describing constant (e.g. ATTEMPTED_TAMPERED_VALUE), not a mystery literal repeated twice.
findings.fix: Extract a private static final String constant (e.g. ATTEMPTED_TAMPERED_VALUE = "Tampered") and use it for both the lastName and city params.

approved_aspects: theVisitCorrectionShouldNotAddASecondVisitToThePet genuinely pins the visit-count invariant: it asserts hasSize(1) on the saved pet's visits after a correction, which would fail if loadPetWithVisit regressed to unconditionally calling pet.addVisit for a visitId-bearing request.

theVisitCorrectionShouldChangeNothingButTheVisit is a real regression test for the @ModelAttribute(name = "owner", binding = false) mass-assignment guard: removing binding=false would let the lastName/city params bind onto the saved Owner and the assertions would fail.

theVisitCorrectionShouldBeRefusedWhenTheVisitIsNotTheNamedPets correctly exercises PRD edge case 3 (cross-pet correction) via a real IllegalArgumentException thrown from findVisit, asserting both the exception and that save was never called.

theVisitCorrectionFormShouldBePrefilledWithTheBookedVisit and theVisitCorrectionShouldUpdateTheVisitInPlaceAndShowTheOwnerRecord cover the prefill and in-place-update acceptance criteria with real assertions on the actual bound/saved Visit object, not mocked-away.
Blank-description and non-future-date refusals are each covered with field-error and error-code assertions plus never(save), correctly pinning PRD's two invalid-correction criteria.
New test names follow the brief's BDD naming school (the{Subject}Should{Outcome}) throughout, matching the PRD's test_names list plus three well-named additions.
AssertJ is used exclusively for assertions (no JUnit assertEquals/assertTrue); four-phase structure with blank-line separation and no phase-comment narration is followed.

OwnerRepository mocking via @MockitoBean is a pre-existing, boundary-appropriate pattern for @WebMvcTest controller slices (persistence is out of the web-layer slice) and is consistent with the rest of the file; not a new mocking-policy violation.
All 12 tests in VisitControllerTests pass under ./gradlew test --tests, confirming the suite is green as reported in the build-pass line.

Dropping the redundant petId parameter removes the drift risk the finding named; no other instance of a caller-supplied id shadowing a value already reachable from the passed object was found in the delta.

The BeforeEach stub rework in VisitControllerTests.java (storedOwner field, findById returning it when set else a fresh graph, save writing it) is a legible, well-commented stateful fake: the comment explains the open-in-view=false rationale for why a reload must observe what save actually persisted. willAnswer(invocation -> this.storedOwner = invocation.getArgument(0)) is a compact but valid idiom (JpaRepository<Owner,Integer>.save returns Owner, and Java's assignment expression yields the assigned value) — readable in context of the preceding comment, no readability finding raised.
ATTEMPTED_TAMPERED_VALUE replaces the two repeated "Tampered" string literals with a named constant, consistent with the file's existing constant-naming style (OWNER_LAST_NAME, OWNER_CITY, etc.).
checkFormat passes clean on the current tree; no formatting violations in the delta.
No new instances of any prior finding's class found on a sweep of the fix-delta surface (VisitController.java, VisitControllerTests.java).

author: doc-reviewer

findings.description: The new mass-assignment bullet states, in its own text, why the exposure is classified an integrity defect rather than a privilege crossing: "because NG-1 already leaves every record open to any caller who reaches the owner-edit page." That causal clause is rationale prose — it explains why the classification holds, not what the open question or its two resolutions are. The PRD boundary rule excludes why; per document-writing's PRD Prohibited Patterns, rationale prose is Critical and belongs in an ADR referenced via a **ADR:** link, not inline in the PRD. It is also never autofix-eligible on this path (prd-authoring/review-checks.md Autofix on the PRD Path, condition 3: PRD-boundary content is a boundary finding, not a style fix). Every other Open Questions bullet in this file states fact or context, never a because-clause defending a verdict; the settled bullet and the never-asked bullet added in this same round both hold to that convention correctly. Trim the because-clause: state the MEDIUM/LOW classification as the reviewer's finding without justifying it inline, or move the justification to an ADR once one exists for this question.

approved_aspects: The settled half of the split bullet at docs/prd.md:186 uses the section's ~~strikethrough~~ Answered <date>: <verdict> convention exactly as every prior resolved entry does, closing the round-1 finding correctly.

The never-asked remainder at docs/prd.md:190 is stated as a genuine open question with no rationale prose, correctly distinguishing settled scope (correction validates as a booking does) from the unasked question (a bypass path of its own).

The expert's choice not to add a Known defect edge case for the mass-assignment finding is correct: every existing Known defect entry (docs/prd.md:74,97,137,169) asserts a stated requirement as the bar being violated, and no requirement currently forbids the write, so a Known defect entry would have prematurely decided the open question.

The mass-assignment bullet's factual description (which handlers rewrite owner contact fields, the MEDIUM/LOW classification, the two resolution paths) carries no internal code references (no class or method names) and correctly leaves the question open rather than resolving it unilaterally.
NG-1 and REQ-VIS-003 references in the new prose resolve to existing rows/anchors in this file.

author: test-reviewer
approved_aspects: Finding 3 resolved cleanly: ATTEMPTED_TAMPERED_VALUE constant now names the tampering value once and is reused for both lastName and city params, matching the Three-Tier Data Naming convention.

Finding 2's rebuttal of the literal 'one shared Owner instance' form is correct: request binding mutates the loaded Visit in place before validation runs, so a single always-shared instance would show refused-values-on-reload even under correct code (hasErrors() short-circuits before save(), but the object graph handed to the view was already mutated by binding). The chosen fix instead ties findById's return value to whatever owners.save() last received, which is the actual persistence boundary this app's mocked-repository model can represent.

Verified by static analysis (not just trusting the implementer's mutation-test claim): with the storedOwner/save() stub, the only way a later findById can return anything other than a pristine ownerWithABookedVisit() is for owners.save() to have been called first. That means any bug the reload assertions in theRefusedVisitCorrectionShouldLeaveTheStoredVisitAsItWas could possibly catch necessarily also calls save() -- so then(this.owners).should(never()).save(any(Owner.class)) in the same test independently pins the identical invariant. The reload lines are not tautological anymore (they now co-vary with a real defect, unlike round 1), but in this mock model they remain logically implied by the never(save) check already present -- not a blocking concern, since the assertions are correct and cost nothing, just an observation that the never(save) check alone would already fail on the same mutation (if(false) on hasErrors) the implementer used to validate the fix; the reload assertion happens to execute first in the test body so it surfaces the failure first.

No order-dependence or cross-test leakage: VisitControllerTests uses JUnit 5's default per-method test instance lifecycle (no @TestInstance(PER_CLASS) present), so the new storedOwner field and its BeforeEach re-stubbing start fresh (null) for every test method -- confirmed by reading the full class for a PER_CLASS annotation and by the 12/12 green run of ./gradlew test --tests VisitControllerTests, which does not depend on method execution order.

savedOwner() (used by theVisitCorrectionShouldChangeNothingButTheVisit and others) uses an independent ArgumentCaptor on owners.save(...), unaffected by and consistent with the new willAnswer stub -- no interaction bug introduced.
Full suite green under this pass's basis: ./gradlew test --tests VisitControllerTests reports 12/12 passing after the fix.
